title: capacity-synthesis-slo-ops-patterns-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines a set of repeatable operational patterns for aligning SLOs, error budget policies, capacity planning, and incident review feedback loops using telemetry-driven simulation. The goal is to reduce repeat incidents caused by under-provisioning or inappropriate SLOs for modern inference workloads (short/long tails, bursty traffic, mixed batch/stream). This is a tactical guide for SREs and platform owners; it complements the SLO governance handbook and capacity playbooks.

Scope

- Services: Redwood API (hosted inference), routing services, batch-queue worker pools, and the request-gateway.
- Audience: SREs, platform engineers, on-call responders, and product reliability partners.
- Not covered: procurement, long-term hardware acquisition schedules (see capacity planning main handbook).

Key concepts and definitions

- Telemetry snapshot: a 72-hour compressed trace of request rates, p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, and KV-cache hit ratios used as a simulation seed.
- Capacity synthesis: automated generation of a minimal viable capacity plan (nodes, instance types, batch sizes) derived from telemetry and SLO targets.
- Hedged capacity: a short-term reserve (10–30%) used to absorb unanticipated bursts without immediate preemption of lower-priority traffic.

Principles

1) Make SLOs actionable: every SLO must map to a concrete remediation path (scale, throttle, fallback model).
2) Close the loop: incident reviews MUST include a simulation of the failure window to validate capacity and error budget assumptions.
3) Simulate before changing SLOs: run what-if analysis using recent telemetry.

SLOs and Error Budget Policies (pattern bank)

- Latency SLO (API generation): 99.9% requests succeed under 300ms for p50 small requests, 99% under 1s for p95 mixed requests.
- Availability SLO (control plane): 99.95% monthly.
- Throughput SLO (batch throughput): meet target batch-processed units per minute with 95% success.

Error budget policy examples

| Severity | Remaining error budget | Automated action | Human review trigger | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Green | > 60% | No change | Weekly review by owner | Normal operating window |
| Yellow | 30–60% | Enable hedged capacity (+15%) | Notify on-call and product | Temporary autoscale policy shift |
| Amber | 10–30% | Start throttling non-critical routes | Pager to service owner (P2) | Reduced prefilling of KV cache |
| Red | < 10% | Apply emergency throttles, rollback recent rollouts | Full incident review (P1) | Consider cross-region failover |

Capacity synthesis workflow (step-by-step)

1) Collect telemetry snapshot
   - Export the last 72 hours of request traces and histograms from TSDB (Prometheus) and distributed tracing (Jaeger).
   - Required metrics: request_count, request_latency_seconds{quantile}, token_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio, gpu_utilization, pod_restart_count.

2) Seed the simulator
   - Compress the trace into a request-rate/time bucket CSV and a latency CDF per bucket.

3) Run base simulation (no hedging)
   - Run 3 scenarios: nominal, +20% sustained, +4x short burst (10s–60s).
   - Output: expected p50/p95/p99, queue lengths, and dropped request rate.

4) Propose capacity delta
   - If p95 > target in any scenario, propose one of: increase instance_count, change instance_type (higher memory for KV cache), or tune batching window.

5) Apply staged change in canary region
   - Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 10 minutes, monitor SLOs and GPU utilization.

6) Roll forward or revert based on metrics within 30 minutes.

Operational tooling and artifact checklist

- Simulation tool: /usr/local/bin/infer-sim (internal) or infer-sim --seed snapshot-2026-02-01.csv --scenario burst --out report.json
- Required dashboards: "SLO Health Overview", "Capacity Synth Results", "Autoscale Actions Log".
- Prometheus queries referenced: 
  - Current p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
  - KV cache hit: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_ratio[1h])

Autoscale policy template (YAML snippet)

apiVersion: autoscale.redwood/v1
kind: HorizontalInferenceAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-autoscale-template
spec:
  targetSLOLatencyMs: 300
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 200
  metrics:
    - type: gpu_utilization
      targetAverageValue: 65
    - type: request_qps
      targetAverageValue: 1200
  hedgedCapacityPercent: 15
  scaleUpCooldownSeconds: 45
  scaleDownCooldownSeconds: 180

Runbook: sudden QoS degradation (for on-call)

1) Triage (0–5 minutes)
   - Check SLO Health Overview and recent Alert channels (#ops-alerts).
   - Run quick simulation with last 5 minutes to confirm if event is traffic-driven or resource-driven: infer-sim --seed live-5m.csv --scenario quick-burst

2) Immediate mitigation (5–15 minutes)
   - If GPU saturation is > 90% and p95 exceeds target: enable hedged capacity via autoscale endpoint: 
     curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://platform.internal/autoscale/enable-hedge -d '{"percent":20, "reason":"oncall-qos"}'
   - If a rollout is in progress: rollback the rollout and move traffic to previous model version.

3) Stabilize (15–60 minutes)
   - Apply throttles for low-priority routes: /tools/route-throttle set --route /embeddings/bulk --rate 0.2
   - Increase sampling for traces to capture full context for post-incident simulation.

4) Post-incident (after stabilization)
   - Create an incident ticket and attach the simulation seed and outputs.
   - Assign to service owner for capacity synthesis run and policy update.

Incident review expectations (SRE standard for this doc)

- Every incident that impacts SLOs must include:
  1) A telemetry snapshot (seed) covering +/- 1 hour around the incident window.
  2) A simulation report that reproduces the observed degradation.
  3) A capacity synthesis proposal (delta and rollback plan).
  4) Action items with owners and due dates.

Metrics and acceptance criteria for runbook changes

- Runbook is updated when a pattern is executed in production and an action item is created in the incident review.
- Acceptance: 30-day reduction in recurrence rate for similar incidents and measurable improvement in error budget utilization (>20% reduction in P1s caused by capacity).
